read: Since yesterday's run, three things mattered most: drug pricing, the market's reaction to the Sanofi-Insmed deal, and a record raise. CMS published round-3 IRA prices: 13 drugs, about 45% net savings, and the first cycle to include Part B. The cuts are deep for Trulicity, Cosentyx and both CDK4/6s. Pharma still rallied. Sanofi rose about 6% on its $41bn Insmed buy and BioSpace framed the sector as a safe haven from tech turmoil, so investors are rewarding big-ticket purchases of commercial growth rather than punishing them. Kymera's upsized $1.75bn follow-on, a record, shows capital is concentrating in oral I&I assets with clean randomized data. The FDA kept acting early: Cogent's Ekitna came about a week ahead of its PDUFA date and Rinvoq got its vitiligo label. Overall tone: risk-on for quality and for large caps. The private market was quiet ahead of US Thanksgiving.

items.headline: Policy: CMS sets round-3 IRA negotiated prices for 13 drugs (first cycle with Part B), effective 1 Jan 2028
items.detail: CMS estimates $9.2bn (45%) net savings against 2025 spend, or about $5.5bn (33%) including the Part D manufacturer discount. Discounts versus 2025 gross cost: Lilly's Trulicity -84% ($150 per month), Boehringer's Tradjenta -83% (first renegotiation), GSK's Anoro Ellipta -72%, Novartis's Cosentyx -67%, BMS's Orencia -57%, J&J's Erleada -51%, Eisai/Merck's Lenvima -46%, Lilly's Verzenio -44%, Novartis's Kisqali -43%, Otsuka/Lundbeck's Rexulti -41%, UCB's Cimzia -37%, Gilead's Biktarvy -37%, Takeda's Entyvio -34%. Pfizer's Xeljanz and Xolair dropped out on generic or biosimilar entry. AbbVie's Botox is excluded under a court order in its suit against HHS. This round brings the total to 37 negotiated drugs. Both CDK4/6s and a large I&I biologic now carry 2028 Medicare price resets.

items.headline: Sanofi / Insmed (update): the market backs the $41bn deal. Sanofi rose about 6% and INSM about 14% on Tuesday
items.detail: What changed is the reaction: the acquirer was rewarded, not sold off. BioSpace says it is 2026's biggest pharma deal by about $30bn and the seventh-largest biopharma acquisition ever. It also notes Lilly rose 3% to $1,406 as pharma traded as a haven. Expect speculation about which mid-cap I&I or respiratory name is next.

items.headline: Bristol Myers Squibb: CFO David Elkins leaves for Coca-Cola; Kevin Dillon succeeds him on 1 March 2027
items.detail: Dillon is SVP and head of corporate finance and business operations, with 11 years at Pfizer before joining BMS. BMS reaffirmed its 2026 guidance. The move comes less than two weeks after CRO Robert Plenge's exit and the merger of all R&D under one leader, so turnover in the top team continues while BMS tries to replenish its pipeline.

items.headline: AbbVie: FDA approves Rinvoq as the first systemic therapy for nonsegmental vitiligo (ages 12+), its 10th US indication
items.detail: Viti-Up at week 48: F-VASI75 was 25% and 23% versus 6% and 7% on placebo; T-VASI50 was 19% and 21% versus 6%. The absolute rates are modest, but the approval creates an oral systemic category in vitiligo and is the first real competition for Incyte's topical Opzelura.

items.headline: Cogent Biosciences: FDA approves Ekitna (bezuclastinib) plus sunitinib in second-line GIST, about a week before the 30 Nov PDUFA
items.detail: In PEAK, median PFS was 16.5 versus 9.2 months (HR 0.50). This is Cogent's first commercial launch, and its second PDUFA (non-advanced systemic mastocytosis) is on 30 Dec. It adds to the run of early FDA actions on clean randomized data.

items.headline: Kymera (update): prices an upsized $1.75bn follow-on at $150.37, a record biotech follow-on
items.detail: Kymera sold 11.64m shares, with closing expected on 25 Nov. The raise is larger than the roughly $1.5bn reported yesterday and fully funds the KT-621 (oral STAT6) Phase 3 build-out.

items.headline: Market: biotech rebounds from near a 60-session low
items.detail: On Monday the NBI rose 4.1% to 7,062.50 and XBI gained nearly 5%, though XBI is still down about 5.7% for November. On Tuesday, large-cap pharma extended gains (Lilly and Novo up about 3%, Sanofi up about 6%).

items.headline: SABCS abstracts are live: J&J's JNJ-0683 (from Ambrx) shows 17.8% ORR in post-Enhertu HER2+ breast cancer; Novartis's SNV4818 shows early promise
items.detail: These are buyout assets with first data before the meeting in early December.

items.headline: DiaMedica: interim DM199 fetal growth restriction data suggest prolonged pregnancy; company raises $86m
items.detail: These are early, small-cohort investigator-sponsored study data.

items.headline: Pharming: interim co-CEOs plan late-stage rare-disease deals with about $100m in cash while a CEO search runs
items.detail: A Phase 2 leniolisib readout in CVID is near.

items.headline: IPO pipeline: BioSpace and PitchBook list five likely IPO candidates, including Ethris, EXUMA and Juvena
items.detail: Biotech IPOs have raised $7.5bn in 2026, but the window is open mainly for larger, well-capitalized companies.

items.headline: Apiary Therapeutics (UBC spin-out) closes a $7.3m seed round for iPSC-derived engineered B cells
items.detail: The cells are designed to produce protein medicines in vivo. Co-led by Genesys Capital and BDC Life Sciences Venture Fund.
